I'm largely new to Lean and this Zulip. I hope post is consistent with community best practice and guidelines. I have been to some talks about Lean. Apologies if this is a bit long.

I want to have a Lean proof of the following: Each simple convex polytope X has a face vector f(X) and a h-vector h(X). Further, h(X) is a linear function of f(X) and vice versa. Further, h(X) is palindromic.

Some background: The palindromic property of h(X) implies what are called the Dehn-Sommerville equations on the face vector f(X). Peter McMullen discovered this proof in 1970. He used shelling of simplicial polytopes. The polar process gives the proof for simple polytopes (the polar of simplicial). Via the moment map applied to toric varieties, this is computing Betti numbers via Morse theory.

Motivation: I have a construction that seems to give an infinite sequence of simple convex polytopes X_0, X_1, X_2, etc and hence h-vectors h(X_i). All being well, each X_i gives F_i which is the sum of the numbers in h(X_i). Further all being well the F_i give the sequence of Fibonacci numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on.

Prior art: I am aware of Topic: Main Theorem of Polytope Theory.

For what I want to do my preferred definition of convex polytope is any image of a simplex under an affine linear map. Further, I don't need real numbers. The rationals are enough. However, I'm open to changing my mind on this.

In this chat archive from 2023 Hyeokjun Kwon writes that they intend to work on this as part of their master's dissertation (if not already done). I've not found this is what happened. The resulting Lean code is available on github here.

This gives me a start for working on my problem. In particular, I now have some Lean code to read and understand and from this learn about how to use Lean.

I now have more than enough to be getting on with. I'm grateful to Hyeokjun Kwon .
I recommend you take a look at this https://github.com/ooovi/Polyhedral
